author: chatgptricks
caption:
Harvard and MIT built 8.3 billion AI personas.

The project is called MatrAIx, a simulation system designed to test digital products on simulated users before real people ever see them. Its Persona 8B database contains 8.3 billion profiles, each described across 1,290 traits covering everything from demographics to preferences and behavior.

These simulated users can take surveys, interact with AI assistants, browse websites, and use apps. Researchers ran 18,189 evaluation trials, including a controlled study where the personas followed their assigned behavioral traits 91.5 percent of the time.

The team has also released about 1 million personas publicly on Hugging Face, while the code is available on GitHub under an MIT license.

This could give companies a new way to test how different types of people might react to a product before launching it.

Would you trust simulated users to predict real ones?
Source: MatrAIx / arXiv

author: superlinked
caption:
OpenAI embedding APIs are standard, but they come with hidden costs: privacy risks, mounting bills, and zero customization. Most teams never even measure if those models work for their specific domain.

The alternative exists. Open models like BGE-M3 and GTE-Qwen2 now match or beat the benchmarks. If you want to stop relying on closed black boxes, check out the SIE repo. It’s built for those who need more control over their RAG applications.

Dive into the code and start contributing. Star the repo here: github.com/superlinked/sie.

Want to talk through your project or suggest a fix? Message the team on LinkedIn. They want the feedback. Open-source only improves when people show up to break things and rebuild them better.

author: nicolejackson45678
caption:
Free AI Alternatives vs. Paid Professional Tools

Here’s a simple one-to-one comparison by use case:

General Assistant: DeepSeek → ChatGPT Plus
Writing & Editing: Kimi → Jasper
AI Research: Perplexity → Scite
Image Generation: PixPix → Midjourney
Video Generation: Jimeng AI → Runway
Knowledge Management: Notion → ClickUp AI
Presentations: Gamma → Beautiful.ai
Data Analysis: ChatExcel → Power BI Pro
Coding Assistant: Tongyi Lingma → GitHub Copilot
Workflow Automation: n8n → Zapier

Free tools are often enough for everyday tasks, while paid platforms usually offer better consistency, integrations, and scalability.

The best tool isn’t always the most expensive one. It’s the one that fits your workflow.
